scope_is: an explicit compatibility rule enforced by tests
per-product security class, SLA and retention
scope_is_not: a data mesh (no federated governance plane)
an event backbone (transport is out of scope; see Phase 12)
a schema registry service (this is a repository of files, versioned in git)

compatibility_policy.rule: A change is backward compatible if and only if it is additive within an existing major version.
backward_compatible: adding a new optional property with a default
adding a new enum value to a property whose consumers are documented to tolerate unknown values
adding a new event_type to manufacturing-events (consumers must ignore unknown types)
breaking: adding a property to the required list
REMOVING a property from the required list (a consumer written against 'this is always present' will fail at runtime, not at validation)
changing the meaning of an existing value
compatibility_policy.version_rule: Major bump for breaking. Minor for additive. Patch for documentation or description-only changes. schema_version in the payload is a string SemVer and MUST match the contract version.
compatibility_policy.why_enum_extension_is_risky: manufacturing-events allows new event types, but only for consumers that already skip unknown types. A consumer that switches exhaustively over event_type must treat a new type as a hard failure, and that consumer is not compatible with the minor bump.

delivery_semantics.consumer_requirement: Deduplicate on event_id. No contract in this registry promises exactly-once delivery.

sla.latency: P95 end-to-end under 5 minutes from occurred_at to availability in the Factory silver layer
sla.measurement: measured at the consumer, from occurred_at, not from produced_at

data_products.grain: one line, one plant-local calendar day, optional shift

sla.latency: published within 24h of period end; late corrections arrive as an incremented revision
P95 under 15 minutes for quarantine events, which gate a physical line
